title: One-Step Simulation with Window Growth
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-alphabet Turing machine with $k>0$ work tapes, choose a source symbol $a_0$, and let $c$ be a source configuration on the retracted input with state $q$. Suppose each work-tape head lies in the integer interval $[a,a+n)$, all tapes are blank at $a-1$ and $a+n$, and Boolean flags $\mathit{left}$ and $\mathit{right}$ correctly record whether the transition moves right at the left boundary and left at the right boundary, respectively. Then the simulator carries the encoding of $c$ and its window to the encoding of the one-step successor configuration and its expanded window: the new window begins at $a-\mathit{left}$ and has length $n+\mathit{right}+\mathit{left}$. This takes $\kappa_k(n,\mathit{left},\mathit{right})$ simulator steps, and during them the work head stays between $z-\mathit{left}\,k$ and $z+1+(n+\mathit{right})k$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: decidable equality on the source alphabet
